title: Two NEOWISE reductions do not establish a common time direction in 20 selected dusty dwarfs
abstract: We test the time direction of 422 NEOWISE visits of 20 published centred dusty-dwarf variables. A signed third-moment statistic favours rapid brightening at six-month separations, but the exact two-sided star-orientation tests give p = 0.128 for all stars and 0.094 for seven field-like stars. A second published reduction gives six-month p = 0.363 for the same 20 stars. One-year tests give p = 0.936 and 0.781. Control-only comparisons give much smaller probabilities, but real controls have a negative time-direction bias. Symmetric flux injections at the target amplitudes raise these probabilities and show that the apparent significance depends on the null model. Pulse injections measure the sensitivity of the test to decay time and event rate. The full sample can detect many of the tested year-long pulse histories; the seven field-like stars have modest power. This result does not establish or exclude collisions as the dust source. We preserve code, aggregate results, source hashes, checks and external retrieval instructions. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-a4564589a191; topic astronomy; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.
